content: When a new function is added to source code but the runtime process (e.g., PM2) is not restarted, the old code continues executing and the new function is never called. Always verify that the running process reflects the latest compiled code after any deployment by checking process logs for expected log messages (e.g., 'Evolution knowledge recorded') and restarting the process if those messages are absent.
summary: Restart runtime process after code changes to avoid stale-code execution
rationale: Evolution #031 documented that recordEvolutionKnowledge was added in a commit but PM2 was never restarted, so every subsequent evolution cycle ran old code and produced zero knowledge files. The root cause was purely operational: new code existed but the process served old code.

content: When a numeric threshold guards a state transition, verify that all legitimate recommendation confidence values exceed that threshold. In this codebase the strategy update gate used `confidence > 0.7` while the 'balanced' recommendation always emitted `confidence = 0.6`, permanently locking the system in 'repair-only' mode. Fix by lowering the gate (e.g., to 0.5) or raising the emitted confidence to a value that actually clears it.
summary: Ensure strategy-update confidence threshold is lower than all valid recommendation values
rationale: Evolution #037 fixed exactly this: getCurrentStrategy() had a 0.7 gate, 'balanced' always produced 0.6, so the system could never advance beyond 'repair-only' even with 0% failure rate. Lowering the gate to 0.5 immediately enabled the strategy transition confirmed by test logs.

content: Self-improvement trigger functions that require a minimum history count (e.g., MIN_HISTORY_FOR_REFLECTION = 3) will silently never fire after data loss or a fresh install. Add a time-based fallback (e.g., force-trigger every 6 hours regardless of history length) so that reflection and metacognitive sessions execute even when the history buffer is below the threshold.
summary: Add time-based fallback triggers for history-gated self-improvement systems
rationale: Evolution #032 found that shouldTriggerReflection() required 3 history records, but after data loss only 1 existed, so neither the reflection nor the metacognitive system had ever been triggered. The fix added an elapsed-time fallback so the systems could operate independently of history depth.

content: When a test file imports a compiled module using a relative path (e.g., `./failure-patterns.js`), the path must point to the actual build output directory (e.g., `../dist/memory/failure-patterns.js`). A mismatched import path causes the entire test file to silently fail to load, reporting zero tests rather than a meaningful error, so always cross-check import paths against the tsconfig `outDir` setting.
summary: Test imports must reference the correct dist/ output path, not a relative sibling path
rationale: Evolution #043 showed the test file imported from `./failure-patterns.js` while the compiled output lived at `../dist/memory/failure-patterns.js`; changing one line enabled 25 previously invisible tests to pass.

content: When TypeScript code uses `fs` or `path` as namespace objects inside a function but only the individual named exports (`existsSync`, `join`) were imported at the top of the file, the compiler emits TS2304 errors at runtime-affecting call sites. Audit all newly added functions for undeclared namespace references and replace them with the already-imported named bindings (e.g., replace `fs.existsSync(path.join(...))` with `existsSync(join(...))`)
summary: Replace undeclared fs/path namespace calls with already-imported named exports
rationale: Evolution #053 caught TypeScript errors in archive-integration.ts where the second half of detectCapabilities() used `fs.existsSync` and `path.join` while only the named exports had been imported, causing compilation failure despite tests passing (tests ran against pre-built dist).

content: Implement span-based tracing by wrapping each logical phase of an agent loop (understand, implement, commit, validate) in explicit `startSpan`/`endSpan` calls tied to a root trace. Without this instrumentation there is no ground-truth audit trail to verify whether an evolution cycle succeeded or failed at a specific sub-step, making post-mortem analysis guesswork.
summary: Wrap each evolution loop phase in explicit span-based trace calls
rationale: Evolution #054 and the Arize research (#045) both established that 'traces are documentation for AI agents' and that without span-level tracing there is no way to pinpoint which phase of a cycle failed. trace.ts was implemented but loop.ts never called it until #054 wired them together.

content: Build a structured capability-tracking module that records what the system can and cannot do, then inject a capability summary into the goal-discovery prompt at each cycle. This provides the LLM with an explicit capability gap analysis so it proposes tasks that expand the weakest dimensions rather than repeating already-mastered skills.
summary: Inject capability-gap summary into goal-discovery prompt to guide task selection
rationale: Evolution #038 derived this from the Alita-G framework: without a capability summary the LLM picks tasks arbitrarily. The implementation created a capability module and updated GoalDiscoveryContext to include capabilitySection, directly influencing which tasks the system proposes.

content: Implement an Experience Distillation pipeline that periodically clusters past interaction trajectories, extracts abstract reusable principles from them via LLM, stores those principles with confidence scores and supporting evidence, and injects the top-ranked relevant principles into the evolution prompt before each decision. This closes the experience→principle→decision loop that plain history storage cannot provide.
summary: Distill past trajectories into abstract principles and inject them into future decision prompts
rationale: Evolutions #047–#052 implemented the full EvolveR Experience Distillation pipeline. The research showed that raw history storage produces only concrete, non-generalizable records, whereas principle distillation yields abstract, reusable guidance that actively shapes future decisions through retrieval and injection.

content: Structure evolution knowledge as GEP-style assets: define named Genes (reusable strategy steps keyed to signal patterns), solidify successful runs into Capsules (with environment fingerprint and blast-radius metadata), and append immutable EvolutionEvents to an append-only JSONL audit log. This transforms ad-hoc prompt adjustments into auditable, replayable assets and prevents redundant reasoning on recurring signal patterns.
summary: Adopt GEP Gene/Capsule/Event asset structure for structured, auditable evolution knowledge
rationale: Evolution #046 researched the EvoMap/evolver GEP protocol and found Jinx lacked signal-driven strategy selection, reusable strategy libraries, and an append-only audit trail. The GEP structure addresses all three gaps while remaining compatible with the existing four-strategy system.

content: Introduce an Agent Archive that maintains multiple parallel evolution branches, each with a fitness score and diversity score, and use a balanced selection strategy (fitness weight 0.6, diversity weight 0.4 by default) when choosing which branch to continue. Automatically spawn a new branch when diversity falls below a threshold (e.g., 0.15) or when all active branches are stagnant, preventing premature convergence to a local optimum.
summary: Maintain a multi-branch Agent Archive to prevent local-optimum convergence in evolution
rationale: Evolution #053 researched Sakana AI's DGM (ICLR 2026) which improved SWE-bench from 20% to 50% by maintaining diverse parallel branches. Jinx had only a single evolution path; the archive implementation (agent-archive.ts + archive-integration.ts) adds branch-level diversity tracking.

content: When connecting to an external API and receiving a validation error (e.g., 'Required at query'), first add any undocumented but commonly required authentication flags (e.g., `useApiKey: true` for Exa) and enhance error logging to capture the full request body and raw response before concluding the API contract has changed. Simultaneously ensure fallback providers (Brave Search, Serper) are configured so the feature degrades gracefully rather than failing completely.
summary: Add auth flags and full-request error logging before assuming API contract has changed
rationale: Evolution #051 diagnosed a 'Required at query' Exa error by adding `useApiKey: true` and detailed logging; the system already had Brave/Serper fallback paths. The principle generalises: unexpected API validation errors often stem from missing optional-but-required fields rather than endpoint changes.

content: When implementing a new MCP-style tool-filtering mechanism (like X-MCP-Tools or tool groups), expose the configuration through an environment variable (e.g., JINX_TOOL_GROUPS) and filter tool registration in the extension layer rather than modifying the core framework. Define named tool groups in a dedicated module so individual sessions can load only the subset of tools they need, reducing per-session context overhead without altering the underlying agent infrastructure.
summary: Filter tool registration via env-var-configured groups in the extension layer, not core
rationale: Evolution #044 analysed GitHub MCP's X-MCP-Tools header and implemented an analogous ToolGroupManager for Jinx. The research confirmed that Pi's 'No MCP' philosophy requires tool-filtering to live in the extension layer, and that env-var configuration keeps the core agent infrastructure stable.

content: Pre-commit hooks that run project-wide lint and type checks will block legitimate single-file fixes whenever pre-existing violations exist elsewhere in the codebase. Establish a clear policy: use `--no-verify` only for documentation-only or one-line targeted fixes when the introduced diff is provably clean (verified by scoped `tsc --noEmit` on modified files only), and track all pre-existing violations in a dedicated issue so they are not silently normalised.
summary: Use scoped type-checking to distinguish new lint errors from pre-existing ones before committing
rationale: Across evolutions #032–#054 the team repeatedly used `--no-verify` to bypass pre-commit hooks because pre-existing ESLint errors blocked unrelated commits. A scoped check strategy would surface only new violations, making `--no-verify` unnecessary and preventing the gradual normalisation of ignoring lint failures.

content: When a metacognitive system is implemented but never invoked in the main execution loop, import its trigger function (`shouldTriggerMetacognitive`) and add an explicit call alongside the reflection trigger inside the loop. Without this wiring, even a fully correct metacognitive module produces zero effect on the system's self-improvement behaviour.
summary: Explicitly wire metacognitive trigger into the main evolution loop alongside reflection
rationale: Evolution #032 found that metacognitive.ts existed and was imported by reflection.ts but was never called from loop.ts. The fix required adding both a shouldTriggerMetacognitive function to the module and an explicit invocation in runEvolutionCycle, otherwise the entire system was dead code.
